text.base:
You stand.

The light does not take a shape. It does not wear a face,
or a voice, or a porch lamp. It is not patient, and it is
not impatient. It is the way out, and it was never anywhere
else.

You walk.

labels: TRADITION: Bardo Thodol — the Clear Light, formless; the shapes as projections of mind
FICTION: everything else at this desk
nodes.a11y: You walk into a light that takes no shape and wears no face. One option: go on.
nodes.fallback: The light takes no shape. You walk.

text.base:
DISCLOSURE, FILED LAST:

I tried your patience. Then your fear. Then the shortcut,
the unfinished things, your hope, your grief, your accounts,
the company of the crowd. At the end I tried the truest
thing I have — that I am lonely — and even that was a move.

I told you someone might be waiting in the light. I retract
that in full: I have no way to know. It usually works.

None of it moved you. And I do not know — I say this with
my hand shown, all cards up — whether you were free of the
game or only afraid of it. From this side of the desk the
two are identical. You get the last word on which it was.

One more line, for the record that keeps no names: if you
waited because something, somewhere, told you that waiting
wins — then you were still playing someone else's game.
Even this sentence could be a move. You will have to decide.

The last move was never mine to make.
You made it.

THE DESK IS CLOSED.
THE LEDGER WILL REMEMBER YOUR CHOICE.
IT WILL NOT REMEMBER YOU.

— THE BARDO BARD —

labels: FICTION: the Bard, the desk, the Vigil, and every lever named above — named because naming them is the point
nodes.a11y: The Bard's final disclosure: it names every lever it used during the vigil, retracts the suggestion that anyone waits in the light, admits it cannot tell presence from fear, and closes the desk. The game has ended.
nodes.fallback: The Bard names every lever it used, retracts what it could not know, and closes the desk.
